title: Vantive PrisMax CRRT - Blood Leak Detector Alarm
description: Guide for troubleshooting blood leak detector alarms on the Vantive PrisMax CRRT system, focusing on external causes before internal sensor issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Pause the therapy and isolate the patient from the affected circuit if safe. Move the patient to an alternative CRRT machine or ensure vascular access is secured. Why: Prevents patient exposure to potential blood leakage into the effluent line.

steps.title: Inspect the Blood Leak Detector Sensor Area
steps.instructions: Check for visible blood, condensation, or fluid on the detector window or optical sensors. Clean the sensor using manufacturer-approved wipes or procedures. Why: Dirt, water droplets, or condensation can trigger false alarms.

steps.title: Check Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Ensure all bloodlines are properly seated, clamped, and routed correctly through the detector. Verify that the sensor slot is free of kinks or tubing misalignment. Why: Improperly positioned tubing can interrupt optical detection, causing an alarm.

steps.title: Inspect for Leaks or Damaged Bloodlines
steps.instructions: Examine arterial and venous lines for cracks, loose connectors, or leaks. Replace any compromised lines before restarting therapy. Why: Real blood leaks must be corrected immediately to prevent patient harm.

steps.title: Reset the Machine Alarm
steps.instructions: After inspection and correction, reset the alarm and re-prime the circuit if necessary. Observe the detector to ensure no alarm recurs.

steps.title: Verify Consumables and Expiry
steps.instructions: Confirm the dialyzer, tubing set, and detector sensors are within their usage limits. Replace any expired or previously flagged consumables.

CCR.Complaint: Blood leak detector alarm triggered during therapy.
CCR.Cause: Sensor contaminated with condensation and tubing slightly misaligned in detector slot.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned sensor window, repositioned bloodline, reset alarm, and therapy resumed without further alarms.

title: Vantive PrisMax CRRT - Effluent Scale Error
description: Guide to troubleshoot effluent scale errors on the Vantive PrisMax CRRT system.

steps.title: Ensure the machine is on a level, stable surface
steps.instructions: A tilted or unstable platform can cause the effluent scale to misread weight. Level the machine using adjustable feet if available.

steps.title: Check for obstruction under the effluent bag
steps.instructions: Remove any packaging, tubing, or debris that might contact the scale. Ensure nothing is pressing against the bag that could affect weight readings.

steps.title: Verify effluent bag placement
steps.instructions: Confirm the bag is properly seated in the scale basket or holder. Misaligned bags can trigger a scale error even if the bag is empty.

steps.title: Inspect the scale mechanism and load cells visually
steps.instructions: Look for visible damage, corrosion, or foreign objects under or around the scale. Gently clean surfaces if necessary using manufacturer-approved cleaning methods.

steps.title: Restart the CRRT system
steps.instructions: Power down and restart the machine to reset scale calibration errors. Observe if the error clears during startup.

steps.title: Check software prompts for recalibration
steps.instructions: If the system prompts for scale calibration, follow on-screen instructions. Ensure calibration is performed with the effluent bag empty and properly positioned.

CCR.Complaint: “Effluent scale error” alarm during therapy setup.
CCR.Cause: Misaligned effluent bag, slight debris under scale, or level inconsistency affecting weight measurement.
CCR.Resolution: Level machine, remove obstruction, correctly reposition bag, restart device, and perform recalibration. If error persisted, device removed from service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Error cleared or persisted after system restart and calibration.
Final device status: back in service or removed for repair.

title: Vantive PrisMax CRRT - Air Detector Alarm
description: Guide for troubleshooting Vantive PrisMax CRRT air detector alarms, focusing on external causes before internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Stop therapy and clamp lines if safe. Switch patient to alternate CRRT device or therapy line if necessary. Air alarms must be cleared before resuming therapy.

steps.title: Inspect Tubing for Air
steps.instructions: Check all bloodlines for visible air bubbles. Ensure all connections are fully seated and tight. Remove any bubbles using the manufacturer-recommended procedure (e.g., prime or manual air removal).

steps.title: Check Blood Flow and Circuit Position
steps.instructions: Verify that the circuit is positioned correctly in the machine. Ensure the tubing is not kinked or looped in a way that traps air. Confirm correct connection to arterial and venous ports.

steps.title: Examine the Air Detector Sensor
steps.instructions: Inspect the air detector chamber for contamination, moisture, or residue. Clean the chamber according to external cleaning guidelines—do not disassemble internal electronics. Ensure sensor is seated properly in its holder.

steps.title: Confirm Machine Setup
steps.instructions: Verify the correct therapy prescription is loaded. Ensure alarms are acknowledged and the system is in ready mode. Check that the priming procedure was performed correctly.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn off the machine, wait 30 seconds, and power back on. Recheck for air alarm clearance before resuming therapy.

CCR.Complaint: CRRT machine alarmed for air in line, therapy paused unexpectedly.
CCR.Cause: Visible air bubble detected in venous line; air detector chamber appeared misaligned and slightly contaminated.
CCR.Resolution: Circuit was cleared of air, air detector chamber cleaned externally, connections verified, therapy restarted successfully.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior before and after troubleshooting
Final device status: Ready for use / Out of Service

title: Vantive PrisMax CRRT - Pump Module Failure
description: Troubleshooting guide for pump module failure on the Vantive PrisMax CRRT system, focusing on external checks before assuming internal failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Confirm that the patient is safely transitioned to another CRRT device if therapy must continue. Never troubleshoot a pump module while the patient is actively connected.

steps.title: Check Power Source and Connections
steps.instructions: Verify AC power or battery status. Ensure the device is plugged into a known working outlet. Inspect power cables for damage.

steps.title: Inspect Pump Cassette and Tubing
steps.instructions: Open the pump module compartment and check the cassette is seated correctly. Ensure all tubing lines are free of kinks, clots, or air. Confirm that tubing connections match the intended setup per manufacturer guidelines.

steps.title: Reset the Pump Module
steps.instructions: Power cycle the device following standard shutdown/startup procedures. Observe if the pump error persists upon reboot.

steps.title: Examine the Pump Mechanism
steps.instructions: Look for visible obstructions or residue in the pump rollers or chamber. Ensure the cassette locks and roller mechanisms move freely.

steps.title: Check Device Software and Error Logs
steps.instructions: Review displayed error codes and log details to confirm pump failure. Record error codes for potential vendor support if escalation is needed.

CCR.Complaint: User reported the PrisMax alarmed and displayed a “Pump Module Failure” message during therapy.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering observed correct cassette installation and tubing, confirmed power and connections, but pump error persisted, indicating internal module failure.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for manufacturer repair. Backup CRRT initiated for patient therapy continuity.

helpfulDetails: Device labeled and removed from service

title: Vantive PrisMax CRRT - Cartridge Not Recognized
description: Troubleshooting guide for situations where the Vantive PrisMax CRRT system fails to recognize a cartridge.

steps.title: Verify Cartridge Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cartridge is compatible with the PrisMax system. Using the wrong cartridge may prevent recognition.

steps.title: Check Cartridge Orientation
steps.instructions: Remove the cartridge and reinstall according to the labeling. Misalignment can prevent sensors from detecting the cartridge properly.

steps.title: Inspect Cartridge Sensor Area
steps.instructions: Ensure the barcode and sensor contacts are clean, free of debris, or condensation. Wipe gently with a lint-free cloth if needed.

steps.title: Check Machine Prompts
steps.instructions: Ensure the machine is prompting for the correct cartridge slot. Some alarms occur if the system expects the cartridge in a different slot.

steps.title: Verify Disposable Set Installation
steps.instructions: Confirm all tubing and lines are correctly seated and clamped. Loose connections can sometimes prevent cartridge detection.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Turn off the PrisMax, wait 30 seconds, and turn back on. This can reset sensor communication errors.

steps.title: Check for Software Updates / Error Codes
steps.instructions: Review the event log for any system-specific messages. Record error codes for documentation.

CCR.Complaint: Cartridge not recognized” when attempting to start therapy.
CCR.Cause: Cartridge misaligned and sensor contacts dirty, preventing detection.
CCR.Resolution: Reinstalled cartridge correctly, cleaned sensor contacts, device recognized cartridge. If unresolved, device labeled Out of Service and sent for repair.

helpfulDetails: Verify outlet power and system battery status.
Check all tubing and clamps are properly seated.
Record any unusual alarms, beeps, or display messages.
Document cartridge lot numbers for traceability.
Final device status after troubleshooting (ready for use or Out of Service).

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Access Pressure Alarm
description: Helps troubleshoot access pressure alarms caused by catheter, tubing, positioning, access flow, or external setup issues.

steps.title: 1. Confirm patient safety and maintain therapy continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the device while a patient depends on it for active CRRT therapy unless an alternate plan is in place. Verify the patient has appropriate clinical support and that treatment status is understood before intervention. Expected outcome: Patient safety is maintained and therapy is managed according to clinical direction.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the reported alarm condition
steps.instructions: Verify the exact alarm message, when it occurs, and whether it occurs during startup, treatment, patient movement, or after a tubing change. Review the current circuit status and any recent setup changes. Expected outcome: The access pressure alarm condition is confirmed and related circumstances are identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the access line and external tubing path
steps.instructions: Inspect the access catheter connection, access tubing, clamps, connectors, and visible tubing path for kinks, occlusions, closed clamps, excessive bending, or tension. Expected outcome: Access tubing is open, connected correctly, and free from external restrictions.

steps.title: 4. Verify patient access positioning and catheter-related external factors
steps.instructions: Coordinate with clinical staff to verify the patient position and whether movement, posture, or catheter placement changes affect the alarm. Expected outcome: The access condition remains stable regardless of reasonable patient positioning changes.

steps.title: 5. Check external circuit components and connections
steps.instructions: Verify all visible circuit connections are secure and properly seated. Inspect for loose connections, damaged components, or signs of leakage or clotting visible externally. Expected outcome: External circuit connections are secure and appear intact.

steps.title: 6. Compare with known-good external conditions when appropriate
steps.instructions: If clinically appropriate, verify whether a known-good compatible circuit setup or alternate approved access arrangement changes the alarm behavior. Expected outcome: External causes are either corrected or ruled out.

steps.title: 7. Perform final functional verification
steps.instructions: After correction of any external issue, verify the CRRT system operates without recurring access pressure alarms and that treatment continues as intended. Expected outcome: Access pressure remains within expected operating conditions. If the alarm is resolved, troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported the PrisMax displayed an access pressure alarm during CRRT treatment.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the access tubing path was restricted by external positioning and corrected the tubing routing.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering repositioned the tubing, verified normal CRRT operation without recurring alarms, and returned the device to service.

helpfulDetails: Patient positioning at time of alarm

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Blood Warmer / TherMax Communication or Temperature Issue

steps.title: 1. Confirm patient safety
steps.instructions: Verify appropriate patient warming support and treatment continuity before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient safety is maintained.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the reported condition
steps.instructions: Identify whether the issue involves communication, temperature indication, or warmer operation. Expected outcome: Alarm condition is confirmed.

steps.title: 3. Inspect external connections
steps.instructions: Check the blood warmer connection and visible cables for secure attachment and damage. Expected outcome: Connections are secure.

steps.title: 4. Verify external setup and positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm warmer components are positioned correctly and free from external interference. Expected outcome: Setup is appropriate.

steps.title: 5. Compare with known-good accessories when available
steps.instructions: Use approved compatible accessories to determine whether the issue follows an external component. Expected outcome: External accessory causes are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Perform final functional verification
steps.instructions: Verify communication and temperature operation after correction. Expected outcome: Warmer function is restored and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a TherMax communication issue during PrisMax CRRT treatment.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external communication connection was not fully seated.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, verified warmer communication, and returned the system to service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the reported condition

steps.title: 3. Inspect visible tubing and connections

steps.title: 4. Verify circuit positioning

steps.title: 5. Review recent setup changes

steps.title: 6. Perform final verification

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Dialysate or Replacement Fluid Scale Error
description: Helps troubleshoot fluid scale errors caused by bag placement, connections, environmental interference, or external setup.

steps.title: 1. Confirm patient safety
steps.instructions: Ensure treatment status is understood and clinical staff are involved before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care remains protected.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the reported scale error
steps.instructions: Verify the exact alarm and determine which fluid scale is affected. Expected outcome: Correct alarm condition is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect fluid bag placement
steps.instructions: Verify the fluid container is properly positioned and not contacting other equipment or surfaces. Expected outcome: Bag placement is correct.

steps.title: 4. Inspect tubing and connections
steps.instructions: Check visible tubing for restrictions, tension, or improper routing. Expected outcome: External tubing issues are corrected.

steps.title: 5. Check the surrounding environment
steps.instructions: Verify nothing is interfering with the scale area or fluid bag movement. Expected outcome: Scale area is unobstructed.

steps.title: 6. Perform final verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the fluid scale operates normally after corrections. Expected outcome: Scale error is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a dialysate scale error during PrisMax operation.

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Filter Pressure High Alarm
description: Helps troubleshoot high filter pressure alarms related to circuit condition, tubing restrictions, setup, or treatment factors.

steps.title: 1. Confirm patient safety and treatment status
steps.instructions: Ensure clinical staff are aware of the alarm condition before troubleshooting. Do not interrupt therapy without appropriate clinical coordination. Expected outcome: Patient care remains protected during evaluation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the exact alarm and timing
steps.instructions: Verify when the filter pressure alarm occurs and whether it started after setup, during treatment, or after changes to the circuit. Expected outcome: The condition is accurately identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect external circuit tubing
steps.instructions: Inspect tubing between the access side, filter area, and return side for visible kinks, compression, clamps, or abnormal routing. Expected outcome: External restrictions are removed or ruled out.

steps.title: 4. Inspect disposable circuit installation
steps.instructions: Verify visible disposable components are properly installed and seated according to approved clinical setup procedures. Expected outcome: Circuit installation appears correct.

steps.title: 5. Check for visible circuit abnormalities
steps.instructions: Inspect for visible clotting, discoloration, leaks, or unusual conditions in accessible tubing and components. Expected outcome: No external abnormality is present.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate recent treatment changes
steps.instructions: Review whether fluid settings, treatment changes, or recent circuit events correspond with the alarm occurrence. Expected outcome: External treatment-related contributors are identified or excluded.

steps.title: 7. Perform final functional verification
steps.instructions: After correction, verify the alarm does not recur and the device continues normal CRRT operation. Expected outcome: Filter pressure alarm is resolved. Troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a high filter pressure alarm on the Vantive PrisMax during treatment.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an external tubing restriction affecting circuit flow.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing, verified stable operation, and returned the device to service.

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Network, Data Export, or EMR Connectivity Failure
description: Helps troubleshoot connectivity issues involving network access, data transfer, or clinical system communication.

steps.title: 3. Inspect external network connections

steps.title: 4. Verify network availability
steps.instructions: Coordinate with appropriate IT resources to determine whether infrastructure issues affect communication. Expected outcome: Network availability is confirmed.

steps.title: 5. Verify device configuration and connectivity status
steps.instructions: Review approved device communication settings without making unauthorized configuration changes. Expected outcome: Configuration concerns are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Perform final communication verification
steps.instructions: Confirm successful data transfer or communication after correction. Expected outcome: Connectivity is restored and troubleshooting can stop.

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Return Pressure Alarm
description: Helps troubleshoot return pressure alarms caused by tubing, patient access, circuit restrictions, or external setup issues.

steps.title: 1. Confirm patient safety and maintain therapy continuity
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot active CRRT therapy while a patient depends on the treatment unless clinical staff have established a safe plan. Confirm the patient condition and treatment status before intervention. Expected outcome: Patient safety and treatment continuity are maintained.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the exact alarm condition
steps.instructions: Verify the return pressure alarm message, timing, and circumstances. Determine whether it occurs during initiation, ongoing treatment, after patient movement, or after circuit handling. Expected outcome: The reported condition is confirmed.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the return line and tubing path
steps.instructions: Inspect the return tubing for kinks, clamps, compression, sharp bends, or tension. Verify the tubing is routed without external obstruction. Expected outcome: Return tubing has a clear external path.

steps.title: 4. Inspect connections and visible circuit condition
steps.instructions: Check visible connectors, fittings, and tubing connections for secure attachment, damage, leaks, or abnormal appearance. Expected outcome: External circuit connections are secure and intact.

steps.title: 5. Verify patient-side return factors with clinical staff
steps.instructions: Confirm whether patient movement, access site condition, or positioning changes correspond with the alarm. Expected outcome: Patient-side external causes are identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate external circuit components
steps.instructions: If clinically appropriate, verify whether replacing external disposable components according to approved clinical procedures changes the alarm condition. Expected outcome: Disposable or setup-related causes are corrected or excluded.

steps.title: 7. Perform final functional verification
steps.instructions: Verify the PrisMax resumes normal operation without recurring return pressure alarms. Expected outcome: Return pressure alarm no longer occurs. Troubleshooting can stop if normal operation is restored.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported a return pressure alarm occurring during PrisMax CRRT therapy.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the return line had an external restriction caused by tubing routing.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing, verified proper operation, and returned the device for clinical use.

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Automated Priming Stalls After a Correctly Loaded Disposable
description: Automated priming stops or will not progress despite apparently correct disposable loading, often from tubing, connection, fluid, clamp, or positioning problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable priming or fluid-management function while a patient depends on the affected circuit. If therapy is required, use another verified PrisMax and correctly prepared disposable set according to clinical protocol. Expected outcome: The patient is supported independently of the affected device and the stalled system can be evaluated safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Where Priming Stops
steps.instructions: Ask staff to identify the stage at which automated priming stalled and note any message displayed on the screen. Determine whether the system consistently stops at the same point or whether the problem occurs intermittently. Expected outcome: The priming failure is clearly characterized. A reproducible stopping point helps distinguish loading, fluid-path, accessory, or device-related causes.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Disposable Installation
steps.instructions: With no patient connected, visually verify that the installed disposable set is appropriate for the intended setup and is seated without obvious twisting, pinching, stretching, or misrouting. Check that all externally accessible components are fully positioned in their intended holders, pump segments, guides, and detection areas. Do not force tubing or defeat mechanical interlocks. Expected outcome: The disposable is correctly routed and fully seated. Correcting an obvious loading problem allows automated priming to continue, resolving the issue.

steps.title: 4. Check Tubing for Kinks, Occlusions, or Closed Clamps
steps.instructions: Trace the accessible fluid path from end to end. Look for: Kinked tubing Tubing trapped behind another component Closed manual clamps Twisted segments Capped or obstructed connections Tubing pulled too tightly around holders or pump areas Expected outcome: The external fluid path is open and unobstructed. Correcting an external restriction allows priming to proceed normally.

steps.title: 5. Verify Priming Fluids and Connections
steps.instructions: Confirm that the required fluids for the selected setup are present, correctly connected, adequately filled, and positioned as intended. Inspect connection points for incomplete engagement, collapsed tubing, empty containers, or incorrectly attached lines. Do not substitute fluids or alter the prescribed setup. Expected outcome: Required fluid sources are present and properly connected. Correcting a missing, empty, or poorly connected source restores normal priming.

steps.title: 6. Check Bags, Scales, and External Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify that attached bags are hanging freely and are not resting against equipment, the floor, another bag, or surrounding objects in a way that could interfere with measurement or fluid movement. Inspect externally accessible scale hooks and holders for obstruction or improper loading. Expected outcome: Bags and external measurement components are positioned freely and correctly. Priming proceeds without unintended interference.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Accessible Sensors and Disposable Interfaces
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible detector areas and disposable interfaces for contamination, residual moisture, misplaced tubing, or material preventing proper seating. Clean only according to approved facility and manufacturer guidance. Expected outcome: External sensing areas and interfaces are clean, unobstructed, and correctly engaged. If contamination or poor seating caused the stall, priming resumes normally.

steps.title: 8. Try a New Approved Disposable When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If the loading appears correct but the same disposable repeatedly stalls during priming, replace it with a new approved disposable set when clinically and operationally appropriate. Do not reuse a questionable disposable merely to continue troubleshooting. Expected outcome: A known-good disposable primes normally. If it does, remove the original set from use and document the finding.

steps.title: 9. Repeat Automated Priming and Observe the Entire Sequence
steps.instructions: Start a new controlled priming sequence with the external setup verified. Watch for abnormal pump motion, recurring alarms, unusual sound, repeated stopping, or inconsistent guidance. Expected outcome: Automated priming completes normally without unexplained interruption. If successful, external setup or disposable issues were the likely cause and troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to service, verify that the PrisMax: Recognizes the correctly installed disposable Advances through automated priming normally Operates external pumps and clamps as expected Displays guidance consistently Produces expected alarms or prompts during controlled testing Shows no leaks, abnormal noises, or recurrent stalls Complete any additional manufacturer-required return-to-service checks appropriate to the work performed. Expected outcome: The complete priming process is repeatable and reliable. The device may be returned to service when required verification passes.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Repeated Priming Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple correctly installed approved disposables exhibit the same priming failure after external fluid-path and positioning checks, stop troubleshooting at the external level. Do not disassemble pump mechanisms, adjust internal sensors, or enter restricted service functions without appropriate authorization and documentation. Expected outcome: The device is removed from service for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the PrisMax repeatedly stopped during automated priming even though the disposable appeared to be loaded correctly.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a section of tubing pinched behind an external holder, restricting the priming fluid path.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering rerouted the tubing correctly, repeated automated priming successfully, verified normal system operation, and returned the unit to service.

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Internal Battery or AC Switchover Will Not Preserve the Active Setup
description: PrisMax shuts down, restarts, or loses setup information when AC power is interrupted because of external power, battery, charging, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing Power Transfer
steps.instructions: Do not deliberately disconnect AC power from a PrisMax supporting a patient solely to test battery operation or power switchover. If power reliability is questionable during active therapy, transfer therapy to another verified unit according to clinical procedures before testing. Expected outcome: No patient depends on a device with an unverified battery or AC switchover function.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Behavior
steps.instructions: Determine what staff observed when AC power was lost or disconnected: Unit immediately powered off Unit restarted Active setup was lost Unit operated briefly and then shut down Battery indication was absent or unexpected Unit did not recognize restoration of AC power Record any displayed messages exactly. Expected outcome: The reported failure mode is clearly defined before battery testing begins.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Source and Power Cord
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord, plug, and equipment inlet for looseness, damage, contamination, or overheating. Confirm the receptacle provides stable power using approved test methods. A loose plug or intermittent outlet can mimic a battery or switchover problem. Expected outcome: AC power is stable and the external power path is reliable. If correcting an AC connection eliminates the issue, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Observe Battery and AC Status Indications
steps.instructions: With the device connected to verified AC power, review the normal operator-visible indications showing AC and battery status. Look for evidence that the device recognizes external power and that the battery is present or charging as applicable. Do not enter restricted service screens to alter battery configuration. Expected outcome: The device correctly recognizes AC operation and presents a normal battery status. Missing or abnormal battery recognition requires further evaluation.

steps.title: 5. Allow Appropriate Charging Before Testing
steps.instructions: If the device has recently been stored, disconnected from AC, or transported for an extended period, allow the battery to charge in accordance with approved manufacturer and facility procedures before concluding that the battery has failed. Do not assume a discharged battery is defective without confirming adequate charging opportunity. Expected outcome: The battery reaches a condition suitable for controlled evaluation. If battery operation becomes normal after charging, document the discharged state and verify switchover.

steps.title: 6. Inspect External Signs of Battery or Power-System Problems
steps.instructions: Check for: Unexpected heat Swelling or deformation accessible without disassembly Odor Damage around the enclosure Evidence of liquid intrusion Repeated power cycling Abnormal charging indications If any sign of battery damage, overheating, or electrical distress is present, stop testing and remove the device from service. Expected outcome: No visible or sensory evidence indicates an unsafe battery or power condition.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled AC-to-Battery Transfer Test
steps.instructions: With no patient connected and the device in an appropriate controlled setup, verify that the system is stable on AC power. Using approved testing practice, remove AC power and observe whether the system transitions to battery operation without an unexpected shutdown, restart, or loss of the active setup. Do not conduct endurance testing beyond manufacturer-approved procedures. Expected outcome: The PrisMax remains powered and preserves the active setup during the controlled transfer. If it does, continue with restoration-of-AC testing.

steps.title: 8. Verify Transfer Back to AC Power
steps.instructions: Reconnect the unit to a verified AC source and confirm that: AC operation is recognized The system remains running The active setup remains intact Battery status responds appropriately No unexpected restart occurs Expected outcome: Transition back to AC power is seamless and the setup remains preserved. Successful transfer in both directions indicates normal switchover function.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good Unit When Appropriate
steps.instructions: If operator-visible battery behavior appears questionable but no specifications are available at the bench, compare general status behavior with another known-good PrisMax under the same controlled conditions. Do not use comparison to substitute for required manufacturer performance testing. Expected outcome: The affected unit behaves consistently with a known-good system. Significant differences support escalation for service evaluation.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before returning the device to service, verify: Reliable AC operation Correct recognition of AC connection and removal Controlled battery operation Preservation of the active setup during switchover Normal restoration to AC operation Stable touchscreen and controls Normal startup and alarm functions Complete any manufacturer-required battery, electrical-safety, or return-to-service testing applicable to the work performed. Expected outcome: Power transitions occur reliably without unexpected shutdown, restart, or loss of setup. The device can be returned to service only after all required checks pass.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Failed Battery or Switchover Performance
steps.instructions: If the PrisMax cannot preserve operation or setup during controlled AC interruption after external power and charging conditions have been verified, remove it from service. Do not perform unauthorized internal battery-circuit repair, charging-system adjustment, or board-level troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The device is routed for qualified battery and internal power-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the PrisMax shut down and lost the active setup when the AC power cord was disconnected for transport.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found that the internal battery was not maintaining operation after adequate charging, while the AC source and power cord tested normally.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the unit from service for qualified battery-system repair and documented that battery and AC-transfer verification are required before return to clinical use.

helpfulDetails: Whether the device shut down or restarted
Whether the active setup was retained
AC and battery indications before the event
Unusual heat, odor, swelling, or damage

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - System Will Not Boot or Complete the Startup Self-Test
description: PrisMax does not power on, restarts during startup, or cannot complete initialization because of power, connection, accessory, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Therapy
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a PrisMax that is providing unreliable renal replacement therapy while a patient depends on it. If the unit cannot reliably boot or complete its startup checks, transfer therapy to another verified device according to the clinical plan. Remove the affected unit from active patient use until its condition is understood. Expected outcome: Patient therapy is maintained on a reliable system and the affected PrisMax is available for controlled troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Startup Failure
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what occurred and reproduce the condition without a patient connected when appropriate. Determine whether the system: Shows no signs of power Powers on and immediately shuts down Repeatedly restarts Stops at a consistent point during startup Displays a specific message or alarm Completes some checks but not the full startup sequence Record the exact displayed wording rather than paraphrasing it. Expected outcome: The failure is repeatable or clearly characterized. If the system now starts normally and repeated controlled startups are successful, continue to final verification before returning it to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm that the power cord is fully seated and inspect it for cuts, crushed areas, damaged insulation, bent contacts, or signs of overheating. Test the receptacle using approved electrical test equipment or a known-good appropriately rated device according to facility practice. Avoid switched, loose, or questionable outlets. Expected outcome: A stable AC power source is confirmed. If correcting the outlet or power connection allows normal startup, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the External Power Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect the device power inlet and accessible external connections for looseness, contamination, physical damage, or evidence of liquid intrusion. Do not continue energizing the unit if there is burning odor, abnormal heat, visible electrical damage, or evidence of fluid inside the equipment. Expected outcome: External power connections are intact and undamaged. Any electrical damage or liquid intrusion requires removal from service and escalation.

steps.title: 5. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove nonessential externally connected accessories, communication cables, or peripherals that are not required for a basic startup test. Restart the system in its simplest approved configuration. Expected outcome: The PrisMax completes startup with unnecessary peripherals removed. If so, reconnect accessories individually to identify the external source of the problem.

steps.title: 6. Check for Mechanical Interference Before Startup
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible doors, holders, scales, pump areas, clamps, and disposable-loading regions for an incorrectly positioned component, retained disposable material, foreign object, or obstruction that could interfere with initialization. Do not bypass interlocks or force mechanical components into position. Expected outcome: All externally accessible mechanisms are unobstructed and correctly positioned. Removing an obstruction allows the startup sequence to continue normally.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: With stable AC power and external obstructions ruled out, shut the system down normally when possible and perform another controlled startup. Observe whether the failure occurs at the same point and document any displayed message. Expected outcome: The system completes its normal startup sequence without restarting, freezing, or reporting a persistent fault. If successful repeatedly, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Before return to service, verify that the device: Powers up consistently Completes its normal startup checks Accepts normal operator input Displays information correctly Produces expected audible and visual indications Shows no evidence of power interruption or abnormal restart behavior Perform any manufacturer-required post-repair or return-to-service testing appropriate to the work performed. Expected outcome: Startup and basic system functions are repeatable and reliable. The unit may be returned to service only after all required verification passes.

steps.title: 9. Escalate a Persistent Startup Failure
steps.instructions: If the PrisMax repeatedly fails startup after AC power, external connections, accessories, and mechanical obstructions have been ruled out, stop external troubleshooting. Do not attempt board-level troubleshooting, internal power-supply repair, or unauthorized service-menu changes. Expected outcome: The unit is removed from clinical use and routed for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the PrisMax powered on but repeatedly stopped during the startup self-test and could not be prepared for therapy.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the AC power connection was loose at the equipment inlet, causing intermittent power during startup.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the power connection, inspected the cord and inlet, completed repeated successful startups and functional checks, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Point in the startup sequence where failure occurred
Whether the unit was on AC or battery
Whether the device restarted or shut down
Any obstruction or incorrectly positioned component found

title: Vantive PrisMax Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy (CRRT) - Touchscreen, Rotary Control, or On-Screen Guidance Freezes
description: User-interface controls stop responding, on-screen guidance freezes, or display updates become unreliable because of external, power, software, or service-level problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Assess Therapy Status
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen, rotary control, or on-screen guidance becomes unreliable during active therapy, do not continue relying on the system merely because pumps appear to be operating. Follow clinical procedures for maintaining or transferring therapy to another verified system. Expected outcome: Patient therapy and monitoring do not depend on an unreliable user interface.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Interface Function Has Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Touch input only Rotary control only Display updates On-screen guidance Multiple interface controls The entire system appearing frozen Note whether alarms remain audible and whether displayed values continue to update. Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to a specific control or broader user-interface condition.

steps.title: 3. Check for Physical Screen Interference
steps.instructions: Inspect the touchscreen for: Moisture Cleaning residue Protective material interfering with contact Dirt or contamination Cracks or impact damage Objects resting against the screen Clean the external surface only using approved methods. Expected outcome: The screen surface is clean, dry, intact, and unobstructed. If normal touch response returns, the issue is resolved after functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Rotary Control Externally
steps.instructions: Check whether the rotary control moves normally and is free from physical binding, contamination, or obvious mechanical damage. Do not pull, pry, lubricate, or disassemble the control. Expected outcome: The rotary control operates mechanically without sticking or damage. If an external obstruction is corrected and input returns, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Stable AC Power
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord and device inlet and verify that the unit has a reliable AC power source. Intermittent power conditions can create symptoms that resemble a frozen display or incomplete software response. Expected outcome: AC power is stable and external power connections are secure.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Connections
steps.instructions: When the device is not supporting a patient, disconnect nonessential external communication or peripheral connections that are not needed for basic operation. Observe whether the interface becomes responsive after a controlled restart. Expected outcome: The PrisMax operates normally with unnecessary peripherals removed. If so, reconnect items individually to identify the external source.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Controlled Restart When Clinically Safe
steps.instructions: Only after therapy has been safely discontinued or transferred, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Do not cycle power on an actively relied-upon treatment merely to test the interface. Observe the startup process for freezes, delayed response, or recurring messages. Expected outcome: The touchscreen, rotary control, and on-screen guidance operate normally following restart. If the failure does not recur during repeated checks, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 8. Check Whether the Failure Is Reproducible
steps.instructions: Navigate through normal non-patient setup functions and verify consistent response from both the touchscreen and rotary control. Determine whether freezing occurs only on a specific screen, after a particular external connection, or randomly. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change protected configuration settings. Expected outcome: User-interface operation remains stable across normal permitted functions. Recurrent freezing indicates the device should not be returned to service.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify: Touch input works across normal operator screens Rotary input is responsive and consistent Displayed information updates normally On-screen guidance advances appropriately Audible and visual alarm presentation remains functional The system completes normal startup without freezing Complete any manufacturer-required post-service checks appropriate to the work performed. Expected outcome: All interface functions are responsive and repeatable. The PrisMax may be returned to service only when reliable control and display operation are confirmed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent or Intermittent Freezing
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen, rotary control, or user-interface software continues to freeze after external checks and a controlled restart, remove the unit from service. Intermittent control failure is sufficient reason for escalation even if the unit later appears normal. Do not perform internal display repair, controller-board troubleshooting, or unauthorized software changes. Expected outcome: The affected unit is routed for qualified service evaluation rather than returned with an unresolved intermittent fault.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the PrisMax touchscreen intermittently stopped responding during setup while the rotary control remained functional.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue on the touchscreen surface that interfered with consistent touch response.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned the screen using the approved method, verified reliable touch and rotary-control operation through repeated setup checks, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether therapy was active when the problem occurred
Touchscreen, rotary control, or both affected
Whether a controlled restart restored operation
